speaker: doctor
text: Good morning. Please sit down. What brings you in today?

speaker: patient
text: Doctor, I have been having a bad cough for about five days now. And since yesterday I have fever also.

speaker: doctor
text: Any chest pain, or difficulty in breathing?

speaker: patient
text: No chest pain. But I feel short of breath when I climb the stairs.

speaker: doctor
text: Is the cough dry, or is there phlegm?

speaker: patient
text: There is phlegm. Yellowish in colour, mostly in the morning.

speaker: doctor
text: Any history of asthma? Do you smoke?

speaker: patient
text: No asthma. I used to smoke, but I stopped four years back.

speaker: doctor
text: Let me check your vitals. Your temperature is one hundred one point two Fahrenheit. Blood pressure is one thirty over eighty five. Pulse is ninety six. Oxygen saturation is ninety seven percent on room air.

speaker: doctor
text: Now let me listen to your chest. Take a deep breath. I can hear some crackles in the right lower zone.

speaker: doctor
text: This looks like a lower respiratory tract infection, most likely bacterial. I do not think it is pneumonia, but I want a chest X ray to be sure.

speaker: doctor
text: It is treatable. I am starting you on Amoxicillin, five hundred milligrams, three times a day, after food, for five days. Please complete the full course even if you feel better.

speaker: doctor
text: For the fever, take Paracetamol six hundred fifty milligrams, only when needed, up to three times a day. Do not take more than that.

speaker: patient
text: Should I take any cough syrup?

speaker: doctor
text: Yes. Two teaspoons at bedtime, for five days. It may make you drowsy, so do not drive after taking it.

speaker: doctor
text: Drink plenty of warm fluids and take rest. If the fever does not come down in three days, or if you get breathing difficulty, come back immediately.

speaker: doctor
text: Otherwise, come for a follow up after one week, with the X ray report.
